units.title: be동사 — 나를 소개하기
units.scene: 처음 만난 고객사 담당자와 인사하는 자리. 이름·회사·역할을 말해야 한다.

think.q: 영어 문장은 왜 '주어 + 동사'가 꼭 있어야 할까?
think.ko: 한국어는 '저 태현이에요'처럼 동사 없이도 말이 된다.
think.en: 영어는 '누가(주어) + 어떻다/무엇이다(동사)'가 뼈대다. '~이다'를 표현하는 동사가 be — I에는 am, 한 명/한 개(he, she, it)에는 is, 여럿·you에는 are.
think.rule: I am · He/She/It is · We/You/They are
ex: I am Taehyun from MZC.
저는 MZC의 태현입니다.
Our office is in Seoul.
저희 사무실은 서울에 있어요.

checks.q: I ___ an account manager.
Our team ___ very small.
checks.why: our team은 '한 팀' — 하나로 보면 is.

checks.q: ___ you the IT manager?
checks.why: you에는 are. 질문은 be동사를 맨 앞으로.

builds.kr: 저는 클라우드 영업을 담당하고 있어요(클라우드 영업 담당자예요).
builds.a: I am a cloud sales manager
She is our engineer

turns.them: Hi, nice to meet you. Are you Taehyun?
turns.why: I 뒤에는 am. 짧은 대답도 Yes, I am.

turns.them: Great. What is your role at MZC?
And who is this?
Tell me a little about your team.
turns.prompt: 팀이 어디에 있고 몇 명인지 be동사로 두 문장 말해 보세요.
turns.model: Our team is in Seoul. We are five people.

units.title: 현재 시제 — 우리 서비스 설명하기
units.scene: 고객에게 우리 회사가 평소에 하는 일을 설명한다. 매번 반복되는 일·사실은 현재 시제.

think.q: '늘 하는 일'을 말할 때 동사 끝에 왜 -s가 붙을까?
think.ko: 한국어는 '저는 지원해요 / 그녀는 지원해요' — 주어가 달라도 동사 모양이 같다.
think.en: 영어 현재 시제는 주어가 he/she/it(한 명·한 개)일 때만 동사에 -s를 붙여 '그 한 명이 한다'를 표시한다. I/you/we/they는 원형.
think.rule: I/We/They support · He/She/It supports · 부정: don't / doesn't + 원형
ex: We manage cloud costs for our clients.
저희는 고객의 클라우드 비용을 관리합니다.
Our engineer checks the system every day.
저희 엔지니어가 매일 시스템을 점검합니다.

checks.q: Our company ___ AWS and Azure.
We ___ 24/7 monitoring.
The tool ___ need extra setup.

builds.a: She sends a cost report every week
We don't manage the contract directly

turns.them: So what does MZC do exactly?
opts: We help companies move to the cloud.
We helps companies move to the cloud.
We helping companies move to the cloud.

turns.them: Who takes care of billing?
turns.a: My colleague handles billing every month

turns.them: Does your team work on weekends?
opts: No, it doesn't, but our on-call engineer does.
No, it don't, but our on-call engineer do.
No, it isn't, but our on-call engineer is.

turns.them: What does your monthly report include?
turns.prompt: 리포트가 무엇을 보여주는지 현재 시제로 한두 문장.
turns.model: It shows your monthly spend and it lists the top five services.

units.title: a / the — 처음 말하는 것과 이미 아는 것
units.scene: 회의실을 예약하고 동료에게 알려준다. 처음 꺼내는 것과 둘 다 아는 것을 구분해야 한다.

think.q: 왜 'meeting room' 앞에 a를 쓰기도 하고 the를 쓰기도 할까?
think.en: 영어는 명사를 말할 때 듣는 사람이 '어느 것'인지 아는지를 표시한다. 처음 꺼내는 하나 → a/an, 서로 이미 아는 그것 → the.
think.rule: 처음·아무거나 하나: a/an · 서로 아는 특정한 것: the · 모음 소리 앞: an
ex: I booked a meeting room.
회의실을 하나 예약했어요.
The meeting room is on the 5th floor.
(그) 회의실은 5층이에요.

checks.q: Can I send you ___ email later?
checks.why: 처음 말하는 하나 + email은 모음 소리 → an.

checks.q: Thanks for ___ quote you sent yesterday.
checks.why: '어제 보낸' 그 견적 — 서로 아는 특정한 것 → the.

checks.q: We need ___ new server.
checks.why: 아직 정해지지 않은 서버 하나 → a.

builds.a: The demo starts at three
I have a question

turns.them: Did you get a room for the client meeting?
opts: Yes, I booked a room on the 5th floor.
Yes, I booked the room on a 5th floor.
Yes, I booked room on 5th floor.
turns.why: 처음 말하는 방 → a room, 층은 특정 → the 5th floor.

turns.them: Great. Is the projector working?
Do we need anything else?
opts: We need an adapter for my laptop.
We need a adapter for my laptop.
We need the adapter for a my laptop.

turns.them: Anything to prepare for the client?
turns.prompt: a와 the를 한 번씩 써서 준비물을 말해 보세요.
turns.model: I will print a short agenda. The client likes paper copies.

units.title: 과거 시제 — 지난주 장애 보고
units.scene: 지난주 금요일에 끝난 장애를 고객에게 시간 순서대로 설명한다.

think.q: 이미 끝난 일을 말할 때 영어는 무엇을 바꿀까?
think.en: 영어는 동사 자체를 과거형으로 바꾼다. 대부분 -ed, 자주 쓰는 동사는 불규칙(go→went, find→found). 질문·부정은 did/didn't + 원형.
think.rule: stopped · restarted · found · went · 부정: didn't + 원형 · 질문: Did ... + 원형?
ex: The server stopped at 3 p.m. on Friday.
서버가 금요일 오후 3시에 멈췄어요.
We found the cause two hours later.
두 시간 뒤에 원인을 찾았어요.

checks.q: Our engineer ___ the system at 5 p.m.
We ___ any data.
___ the alert go to your team?

builds.a: We fixed the service at five
The customer data didn't change

turns.them: What happened last Friday?
opts: The database went down at 3 p.m.
The database goes down at 3 p.m.
The database go down at 3 p.m.

turns.them: When did you find the cause?
turns.a: We found it two hours later

turns.them: Did you lose any data?
opts: No, we didn't lose any data.
No, we didn't lost any data.
No, we don't lost any data.

turns.them: What did your team do after that?
turns.prompt: 그 다음 한 조치 두 가지를 과거 시제로.
turns.model: We added more monitoring and we tested the backup system.

units.title: will vs be going to — 약속과 계획
units.scene: 미팅 끝에 '지금 결정한 약속'과 '이미 정해둔 계획'을 구분해 말한다.

think.q: 둘 다 '~할 거예요'인데 영어는 왜 두 가지일까?
think.ko: 한국어는 '보낼게요 / 보낼 예정이에요'를 대충 섞어 쓴다.
think.en: will = 말하는 지금 정한 약속·제안(I'll send it). be going to = 이미 정해 둔 계획(We're going to migrate next month).
think.rule: 즉석 결정·약속: I'll + 원형 · 이미 정한 계획: be going to + 원형
ex: I'll send you the slides today.
오늘 슬라이드 보내드릴게요.(지금 약속)
We're going to launch the pilot in May.
5월에 파일럿을 시작할 예정이에요.(정해진 계획)

checks.q: A: The file is too big. B: No problem, I ___ share a link.
checks.why: 방금 문제를 듣고 정한 해결 → will.

checks.q: We ___ move to the new office next month. It's all planned.
I ___ call you back in ten minutes.

builds.a: I will check it tomorrow

builds.kr: (계획) 저희는 다음 주에 데이터를 옮길 예정이에요.
builds.a: We are going to move the data next week

turns.them: Can you send the updated quote?
opts: Sure, I'll send it this afternoon.
Sure, I'm sending it this afternoon yesterday.
Sure, I send it this afternoon.
turns.why: 요청을 듣고 바로 하는 약속 → I'll.

turns.them: What's the plan for the migration?
turns.a: We are going to start in June
turns.why: 이미 세운 계획 → be going to.

turns.them: Our CFO has questions about pricing.
opts: I'll prepare a short cost summary for her.
I'm going prepare a short cost summary for her.
I prepare a short cost summary for her tomorrow ago.
turns.why: 방금 들은 문제에 대한 즉석 제안 → I'll + 원형.

turns.them: So what are the next steps?
turns.prompt: 정해진 계획(be going to) 하나와 지금 하는 약속(will) 하나.
turns.model: We are going to run a pilot next month, and I'll send you the schedule tomorrow.

units.title: 비교급·최상급 — 요금제 비교
units.scene: 고객에게 두 요금제를 비교해 설명하고 가장 알맞은 것을 추천한다.

think.ko: 한국어는 '더'만 붙이면 된다: 더 싸다, 더 안정적이다.
think.en: 짧은 형용사는 끝에 -er(cheaper), 긴 형용사는 앞에 more(more stable). 비교 대상은 than. 셋 이상 중 1등은 the -est / the most.
think.rule: cheap→cheaper→the cheapest · stable→more stable→the most stable · good→better→the best
ex: Plan B is cheaper than Plan A.
B 요금제가 A보다 싸요.
This is the most flexible option.
이게 가장 유연한 옵션이에요.

checks.q: The Seoul region is ___ than the US region for you.
Reserved instances are ___ than on-demand.
This is ___ secure option we have.
checks.why: 여러 개 중 1등, 긴 형용사 → the most secure.

builds.a: This plan is more flexible than that one
This is the best choice

turns.them: What's the difference between the two plans?
opts: Plan B is cheaper, but Plan A is more flexible.
Plan B is more cheap, but Plan A is flexibler.
Plan B is cheapest than Plan A.

turns.them: Which one is better for us?
turns.a: Plan B is better for your budget

turns.them: Is there anything even cheaper?
opts: The three-year plan is the cheapest option.
The three-year plan is the most cheap option.
The three-year plan is cheaper option.

turns.them: So what do you recommend?
turns.prompt: 비교급 하나(than)와 최상급 하나로 추천 이유를 말해 보세요.
turns.model: The one-year plan is safer than the three-year plan, and it is the most flexible option for you.

units.title: can / could — 정중하게 요청하기
units.scene: 고객에게 자료를 부탁하고, 우리가 할 수 있는 것을 말한다. 거절도 정중하게.

think.q: 왜 원어민은 '보내 주세요'를 'Could you send ...?'라고 물을까?
think.en: 영어의 공손함은 명령문이 아니라 질문 + could에서 나온다. could는 can보다 한 걸음 물러선 말투. 뒤에는 항상 동사원형.
think.rule: Could you + 원형 ...? (공손한 요청) · I can / can't + 원형 (능력·가능)
ex: Could you share last month's invoice?
지난달 청구서를 공유해 주실 수 있을까요?
We can set it up in two days.
이틀 안에 설정해 드릴 수 있어요.

checks.q: Could you ___ me the login details?
(고객에게 공손하게) ___ you check the budget with your CFO?
Sorry, we ___ change the price this quarter.

builds.kr: 회의 일정을 옮겨 주실 수 있을까요?
builds.a: Could you move the meeting

builds.kr: 저희가 무료로 교육을 제공할 수 있어요.
builds.a: We can provide free training

turns.them: We want to start the PoC soon.
opts: Great. Could you share your architecture diagram?
Great. Share me your architecture diagram.
Great. Could you shared your architecture diagram?

turns.them: How fast can you set up the environment?
turns.kr: 환경을 얼마나 빨리 설정할 수 있어요?
turns.a: We can set it up this week

turns.them: Can you give us a 50% discount?
opts: I'm afraid we can't, but we can offer free support.
No, we don't can, but we can to offer free support.
turns.why: I'm afraid로 완충 + can't / can + 원형.

turns.them: Anything else you need from us?
turns.prompt: Could you로 공손하게 두 가지를 부탁해 보세요.
turns.model: Could you send us your current bill, and could you invite your security team to the next call?

units.title: 현재완료 — '지금까지' 이어진 일
units.scene: 장애가 아직 계속되는 중. 언제부터였는지, 지금까지 무엇을 했는지 보고한다.

think.q: '어제 멈췄다'와 '어제부터 멈춰 있다'는 영어로 어떻게 다를까?
think.ko: 한국어는 둘 다 과거처럼 말하고 '-부터'로 구분한다.
think.en: 과거형은 끝난 일(stopped yesterday). 현재완료(have p.p.)는 과거에 시작해 '지금도' 영향이 있는 일. since + 시작 시점, for + 기간.
think.rule: It has been down since 9 a.m. · We have tried three fixes so far · 끝난 시점(yesterday, at 3)과는 과거형
ex: The API has been slow since this morning.
오늘 아침부터 API가 느려요(지금도).
We have already contacted AWS support.
AWS 지원팀에 이미 연락했어요.

checks.q: The service ___ unstable since Monday.
We ___ the root cause yesterday at 5 p.m.
I've worked with this client ___ three years.

builds.kr: 저희는 지금까지 두 가지 해결책을 시도했어요.
builds.a: We have tried two fixes so far
This issue has existed since last week

sim.who: 고객사 CTO (Mr. Lim) — 화가 난 상태

turns.them: How long has the system been down?
opts: It has been down since 9 a.m.

turns.them: What have you done so far?
turns.a: We have restarted all the servers

turns.them: When did you tell the vendor?
Has this happened before?
turns.prompt: 경험(현재완료) 한 문장 + 끝난 과거 한 문장으로 답해 보세요.
turns.model: It has happened once before. We fixed it in about an hour last year.

units.title: 1조건문 — 협상에서 조건 걸기
units.scene: 월말 계약 협상. '이번 달에 서명하면 ~해 드릴게요'처럼 실제로 가능한 조건을 제시한다.

think.q: '이번 달에 계약하시면'은 미래인데 왜 영어는 현재형(sign)을 쓸까?
think.en: 영어는 if절 안에서는 미래도 현재형으로 쓰고, 결과 쪽에만 will을 둔다. 조건(현재) → 결과(will). 현실적으로 일어날 수 있는 조건.
think.rule: If you sign this month, we will add free training. (If절에 will 금지)
ex: If you commit for a year, we'll lower the rate.
1년 약정하시면 요율을 낮춰 드릴게요.
If the pilot goes well, we'll expand it.
파일럿이 잘 되면 확대할 거예요.

checks.q: If you ___ the contract today, we'll start next week.
If the budget is approved, we ___ the project in May.
We'll give you a discount if you ___ for two years.

builds.a: If you commit for three years you will save twenty percent
I will tell you if it gets approved

turns.them: Your price is still too high for us.
opts: If you sign this month, we'll include free training.
If you will sign this month, we include free training.
If you signed this month, we'll include free training.

turns.them: What if we need more time?
turns.a: If you need more time we will extend the offer
turns.why: if절 현재 need, 결과 will extend.

turns.them: Will you lower the price if we commit for two years?
opts: Yes, if you commit for two years, we'll lower it by 10%.
Yes, if you will commit for two years, we lower it by 10%.
Yes, if you committed for two years, we lowered it by 10%.

turns.them: Okay, give me your best offer.
turns.prompt: If ~, we will ~ 로 조건 두 개를 걸어 제안해 보세요.
turns.model: If you sign by Friday, we will add a month of free support, and if you commit for two years, we will lower the rate by ten percent.

units.title: 관계대명사 — 제품을 한 문장으로 설명
units.scene: 데모 중에 기능과 사람을 '~하는 무엇/누구'로 풀어서 설명한다.

think.q: '비용을 모니터링하는 도구'를 영어는 어떤 순서로 말할까?
think.ko: 한국어는 꾸미는 말이 앞에 온다: [비용을 모니터링하는] 도구.
think.en: 영어는 명사를 먼저 말하고 뒤에서 설명을 붙인다: a tool [that monitors costs]. 사물은 that/which, 사람은 who/that.
ex: We use a tool that monitors your cloud costs.
클라우드 비용을 모니터링하는 도구를 씁니다.
She's the engineer who built the dashboard.
그분이 대시보드를 만든 엔지니어예요.

checks.q: This is the feature ___ sends daily alerts.
I'll introduce you to the manager ___ handles billing.
The report ___ you asked for is ready.

builds.kr: 저희는 비용을 줄여 주는 서비스를 제공해요.
builds.a: We offer a service that reduces costs
He is the person who manages the contract

turns.them: What is this dashboard?
opts: It's a dashboard that shows your daily spend.
It's a dashboard who shows your daily spend.
It's a dashboard shows that your daily spend.

turns.them: Who can I contact for billing questions?
turns.a: You can contact Jina who manages billing

turns.them: Is this the report we discussed last week?
opts: Yes, it's the report that we discussed.
Yes, it's the report who we discussed.
Yes, it's the report we discussed it.

turns.them: What makes your service different?
turns.prompt: that 또는 who를 넣은 문장 두 개로 차별점을 설명해 보세요.
turns.model: We have a tool that finds idle servers, and a team who reviews your bill every month.

units.title: 수동태 — '누가'보다 '무엇이'가 중요할 때
units.scene: 청구·처리 상황을 보고한다. 누가 했는지보다 일이 처리됐다는 사실이 중요하다.

think.ko: 한국어는 주어를 자주 생략한다: '(누가) 어제 보냈어요'.
think.en: 영어는 주어를 생략할 수 없다. 행위자가 중요하지 않으면 대상을 주어로 세우고 be + p.p.로 말한다.
think.rule: The invoice was sent yesterday. · The issue is being fixed now. · The credit will be applied next month.
ex: Your refund was processed on Monday.
환불은 월요일에 처리됐어요.
The report is generated every morning.
리포트는 매일 아침 생성돼요.

checks.q: The invoice ___ yesterday.
Your account ___ every month.
The credit ___ to your next bill.

builds.a: The fee is charged on the first of every month
The problem was solved this morning

turns.them: I haven't received the invoice.
opts: It was sent to your old email address.
It sent to your old email address.
It was send to your old email address.

turns.them: Why is this month's bill so high?
turns.a: Extra storage was added last week
turns.why: 누가 추가했는지보다 추가된 사실 → was added.

turns.them: Will the overcharge be refunded?
opts: Yes, it will be refunded next month.
Yes, it will refunded next month.

turns.them: How is the data protected?
turns.prompt: 수동태 두 문장으로 보호 방식을 설명해 보세요.
turns.model: All data is encrypted, and backups are stored in a separate region.

units.title: 2·3조건문 — 가정과 회고
units.point: If + 과거 → would · If + had p.p. → would have p.p.
units.scene: 지금 사실이 아닌 가정으로 협상하고(2조건문), 지난 장애를 회고한다(3조건문).

think.q: '예산이 더 있다면' — 실제로는 없는데 왜 과거형(had)을 쓸까?
think.en: 영어는 시제를 한 칸 과거로 밀어 '현실과 거리가 있다'를 표시한다. 지금의 비현실 → If + 과거, would + 원형. 과거의 비현실(이미 지나간 일) → If + had p.p., would have p.p.
think.rule: If we had more budget, we would expand. · If we had set alerts, we would have caught it.
ex: If we were your only vendor, we would give you a better rate.
저희가 유일한 벤더라면 더 좋은 요율을 드릴 텐데요.
If we had tested the backup, we would have recovered faster.
백업을 테스트했더라면 더 빨리 복구했을 거예요.

checks.q: If we ___ more engineers, we would finish sooner. (실제로는 없다)
If you had called us earlier, we ___ the issue.
checks.why: 지나간 일의 가정 → would have p.p.

checks.q: If I ___ you, I would choose the one-year plan.

builds.kr: 시간이 더 있다면 전부 옮길 텐데요.
builds.a: If we had more time we would migrate everything
If we had set alerts we would have caught the problem

turns.them: Could you do this for half the price?
opts: If we cut the price that much, we would have to remove support.
If we will cut the price that much, we have to remove support.
If we cut the price that much, we will had to remove support.
turns.why: 비현실 가정 → if + 과거, would + 원형.

turns.them: Last quarter's outage cost us a lot.
turns.a: If we had set up alerts we would have caught it early
turns.why: 지난 일 가정 → had p.p. / would have p.p.

turns.them: What would you do in my position?
opts: If I were you, I would start with a small pilot.
If I am you, I will start with a small pilot.
If I was you, I would started with a small pilot.
turns.why: If I were you, I would + 원형.

turns.them: Why should we trust you this time?
turns.prompt: 3조건문으로 과거 반성 한 문장 + 1조건문으로 앞으로의 약속 한 문장.
turns.model: If we had monitored the database, we would have prevented the outage. If you renew, we will add 24/7 monitoring.

units.title: 간접화법 — 회의 결과를 전달하기
units.scene: 고객 미팅에서 들은 말을 내부 팀에게 정확히 전달한다.

think.q: 고객이 'We will decide by Friday'라고 했다. 팀에게 전할 때 왜 will이 would가 될까?
think.ko: 한국어는 '금요일까지 결정한대요'로 원래 말을 거의 그대로 옮긴다.
think.en: 영어는 '말한 시점(과거)'에 맞춰 전하는 문장의 시제를 한 칸 뒤로 옮긴다: will→would, is→was, can→could. 질문은 asked if/whether + 평서문 어순.
think.rule: She said (that) they would decide by Friday. · He asked if we could lower the price.
ex: The CTO said they were happy with the pilot.
CTO가 파일럿에 만족한다고 했어요.
She asked whether we could start in May.
5월에 시작할 수 있는지 물었어요.

checks.q: "We need more time." → She said they ___ more time.
"Can you send the quote?" → He asked if we ___ the quote.
He asked ___ the price included support.

builds.a: She said they would decide by Friday

builds.kr: CTO가 저희가 5월에 시작할 수 있는지 물었어요.
builds.a: The CTO asked if we could start in May

sim.who: 우리 팀 매니저 (Daniel) — 회의 결과 보고

turns.them: So what did the client say about the budget?
opts: She said the budget was already approved.
She said the budget is already approve.
She said me the budget was already approved.
turns.why: said + 과거(was approved). said 뒤에 me 없음(told me는 가능).

turns.them: Did they ask anything about security?
turns.a: They asked if we had ISMS certification
turns.why: asked if + 평서문 어순 + 시제 한 칸 뒤.

turns.them: When will they decide?
opts: He told me they would decide next week.
He said me they will decide next week.
He told they would decided next week.

turns.them: Anything else I should know?
turns.prompt: 고객이 한 말 두 가지를 said / asked if 로 전달해 보세요.
turns.model: The CFO said they wanted a three-year option, and she asked if we could include training.

units.title: 간접의문문 — 임원에게 정중하게 묻기
units.point: Could you tell me + 의문사 + 주어 + 동사
units.scene: 고객사 임원에게 민감한 질문(예산·일정·결정권자)을 정중하게 던진다.

think.q: 'When does the contract end?'를 부드럽게 바꾸면 왜 어순이 변할까?
think.ko: 한국어는 '계약이 언제 끝나는지 여쭤봐도 될까요?' — 어순이 그대로다.
think.en: 질문을 다른 문장 안에 넣으면 더 이상 질문 어순이 아니다: Could you tell me [when the contract ends]? — 의문사 + 주어 + 동사(do/does 없음).
think.rule: Do you know who makes the final decision? · I was wondering when you plan to launch.
ex: Could you tell me when the current contract ends?
현재 계약이 언제 끝나는지 알려 주실 수 있을까요?
Do you know who approves the budget?
예산은 누가 승인하는지 아세요?

checks.q: Could you tell me when ___?
Do you know who ___ the final decision?
I was wondering ___ you have a budget for this.

builds.kr: 누가 최종 결정을 하시는지 여쭤봐도 될까요?
builds.a: Could you tell me who makes the final decision
I was wondering when you plan to launch

turns.them: We're interested, but it's early days.
opts: Could you tell me when you plan to decide?
Could you tell me when do you plan to decide?
Could you tell me when plan you to decide?

turns.them: The budget isn't fully set yet.
turns.a: Do you know who approves the budget

turns.them: We might go with another vendor.
opts: I was wondering what matters most to you in this decision.
I was wondering what does matter most to you.
I was wondering what matters most to you in this decision?
turns.why: 평서문 속 질문 — 물음표 없이, 주어+동사.

turns.them: Any other questions?
turns.prompt: Could you tell me / Do you know 로 정중한 질문 두 개.
turns.model: Could you tell me how many users you have now, and do you know when your current contract ends?

units.title: 현재완료진행 — 계속해 온 노력 강조
units.scene: 진행 상황 보고. '몇 주째 계속 하고 있다'는 과정과 노력을 보여준다.

think.q: '3주째 테스트하고 있어요'는 have tested일까, have been testing일까?
think.en: have + p.p.는 결과(몇 개를 끝냈다), have been + -ing는 지금까지 계속되는 과정(얼마나 오래 해왔다). 기간(for/since)과 잘 어울린다.
think.rule: We've been testing it for three weeks. (과정) · We've tested 20 cases. (결과·개수)
ex: Our team has been working on the migration since March.
3월부터 계속 마이그레이션 작업을 하고 있어요.
We've migrated 12 of 20 services.
20개 중 12개를 옮겼어요.

checks.q: We ___ the new dashboard for two weeks.
So far we ___ 30 bugs.
How long ___ you been working with AWS?

builds.a: We have been optimizing costs since January
We have moved fifteen servers so far

sim.who: 고객사 PM (Mr. Ahn) — 주간 진행 회의

turns.them: How is the migration going?
opts: We've been moving the databases all week.
We are moving the databases since Monday.
We've been move the databases all week.
turns.why: 이번 주 내내 계속 → have been -ing.

turns.them: How many services are done?
Why is it taking so long?
opts: We've been waiting for security approval since Tuesday.
We wait for security approval since Tuesday.
We've waited for security approval since Tuesday ago.
turns.why: 화요일부터 계속 기다리는 중 → have been waiting.

turns.them: Give me a quick summary.
turns.prompt: 계속해 온 것(have been -ing) 하나 + 끝낸 결과(have p.p.) 하나.
turns.model: We have been testing the new setup for two weeks, and we have fixed most of the issues.
turns.focus: present perfect continuous vs present perfect

units.title: 헤징 — 단정하지 않고 설득하기
units.scene: 고객의 계획에 동의하지 않지만 관계를 해치지 않고 대안을 제시한다.

think.q: 원어민은 반대할 때 왜 'You're wrong' 대신 'It might be worth ...'라고 할까?
think.ko: 한국어는 '~인 것 같아요', '~하면 어떨까요'로 완곡하게 말한다.
think.en: 영어도 같다 — 단정 대신 가능성 조동사(might, could), 인상 동사(seem, appear), 경향(tend to), 수량 완충(a bit, somewhat)으로 '제안'의 틀을 만든다. 말하는 사람의 확신 정도를 조절하는 문법.
think.rule: It might be worth -ing · It seems (that) ... · That could be a risk · tend to + 원형
ex: It might be worth testing this with a smaller workload first.
먼저 작은 워크로드로 테스트해 보는 것도 좋을 것 같아요.
That approach seems a bit risky for a production system.
그 방식은 운영 시스템에는 조금 위험해 보여요.

checks.q: (부드럽게 반대) That plan ___ a little ambitious for Q1.
It might be worth ___ a pilot first.
Large migrations ___ take longer than planned.

builds.kr: 먼저 비용을 검토해 보는 게 좋을 수도 있어요.
builds.a: It might be worth reviewing the costs first
The timeline seems a bit tight

sim.who: 고객사 CIO (Mr. Nam) — 무리한 일정을 고집

turns.them: We want to move everything in one month.
turns.kr: 한 달 안에 전부 옮기고 싶어요.
opts: That seems quite ambitious. It might be worth phasing it.
That is impossible. You are wrong.
That must be definitely too fast.

turns.them: Our team is very experienced.
turns.a: Even experienced teams tend to need more time

turns.them: So you think we'll fail?
opts: Not at all. I'd just suggest that a two-phase plan could reduce the risk.
Yes, I think you will fail.
I suggest you to reduce the risk.
turns.why: I'd suggest that + could로 제안 틀.

turns.them: What would you propose?
turns.prompt: might/could/seem 중 두 개 이상을 써서 대안을 제안해 보세요.
turns.model: It might be worth moving the non-critical systems first. That could give your team time to learn the tools, and it seems safer for your customers.

units.title: 강조 구문 — 핵심을 앞으로
units.point: What ~ is · It is ~ that · Not only did ~
units.scene: 임원 보고에서 한 문장으로 핵심을 꽂는다. 무엇을 강조하느냐에 따라 문장 구조를 바꾼다.

think.q: '가장 중요한 건 속도예요'를 영어는 왜 What으로 시작할까?
think.en: 영어는 문장 뼈대를 바꿔 강조한다. What + 주어 + 동사 + is + 강조 대상 / It is + 강조 대상 + that ... / 부정어를 앞에 두면 도치(Not only did we ...).
think.rule: What matters most is speed. · It was the monitoring that saved us. · Not only did we cut costs, but we also ...
ex: What your team needs is visibility, not more tools.
팀에 필요한 건 도구가 아니라 가시성이에요.
Not only did we reduce costs, but we also improved uptime.
비용을 줄였을 뿐 아니라 가용성도 높였어요.

checks.q: ___ we need is a clear owner.
It was the security team ___ found the issue.
Not only ___ costs, but we also saved time.
checks.why: 부정어가 앞으로 → 도치 did we cut.

builds.a: What we propose is a phased transition

builds.kr: 장애를 막은 건 바로 자동 백업이었어요.
builds.a: It was the automatic backup that prevented the outage

turns.them: Give me the one thing I should remember.
opts: What you'll get is a 30% cost reduction within six months.
That you'll get is a 30% cost reduction.
What will you get is a 30% cost reduction.

turns.them: Why did the last project succeed?
turns.a: It was the weekly review that made the difference

turns.them: What did we actually gain?
opts: Not only did we cut costs, but we also improved security.
Not only we cut costs, but we also improved security.
Not only did we cut costs, but also we improved security did.

turns.them: Why should I choose you?
turns.prompt: What ~ is 와 It is ~ that 중 하나 이상으로 핵심을 말해 보세요.
turns.model: What sets us apart is our monthly FinOps review. It is that discipline that keeps your costs down.
turns.focus: cleft sentences and inversion for emphasis

units.title: 분사구문 — 보고서 문장을 압축하기
units.scene: 사후 분석(포스트모템) 보고서를 쓴다. 원인·조치를 짧고 매끄럽게 이어야 한다.

think.q: '로그를 검토한 후 우리는 원인을 찾았다'를 영어는 어떻게 한 덩어리로 줄일까?
think.en: 두 절의 주어가 같으면 앞 절을 분사로 줄인다. 동시·이유 → -ing, 먼저 끝난 일 → Having + p.p. 주절의 주어가 분사의 행위자여야 한다(dangling 금지).
think.rule: Having reviewed the logs, we identified the root cause. · Working with AWS, we restored the service in an hour.
ex: Having analyzed the bill, we found three idle databases.
청구서를 분석한 뒤 유휴 DB 3개를 찾았습니다.
Using reserved instances, the client saved 30%.
예약 인스턴스를 활용해 고객은 30%를 절감했습니다.

checks.q: ___ the logs, we found the error.
___ closely with the vendor, we fixed it in two hours.
Having reviewed the plan, ___

builds.kr: 설정을 바꾼 뒤, 저희는 지연 시간을 절반으로 줄였습니다.
builds.a: Having changed the settings we cut latency in half

builds.kr: 자동 알림을 사용해 팀이 문제를 더 빨리 잡았습니다.
builds.a: Using automatic alerts the team caught the issue faster

sim.who: 우리 회사 임원 (Director Kim) — 포스트모템 리뷰

turns.them: How did you find the root cause?
opts: Having reviewed the access logs, we found a misconfigured rule.
Reviewed the access logs, we found a misconfigured rule.
Having reviewed the access logs, a misconfigured rule was found by it.

turns.them: How did you restore service so quickly?
turns.a: Working with the vendor we restored it in an hour

turns.them: What will prevent a repeat?
opts: Having added automated checks, we can now catch this in minutes.
Added automated checks, we can now catch this in minutes.
Having add automated checks, we can now catch this.

turns.them: Summarize it in two sentences for the client.
turns.prompt: 분사구문(Having p.p. 또는 -ing)을 넣어 두 문장으로 요약해 말해 보세요.
turns.model: Having identified a faulty rule, we fixed it within an hour. Using new automated checks, we will now detect similar issues in minutes.
turns.focus: participle clauses (having p.p., -ing) with matching subject
